messages.subject: [R-sig-hpc] ff package Help
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lucas,

the examples below give you an idea how to add a column to an ffdf.

library(ff)

# physically single columns
x<-ff(runif(10,0,1))
y<-ff(runif(10,-1,1))
z<-ff(runif(10,2,3))
fdata<-ffdf(x,y,z)
a <- clone(x)
fdata2 <- do.call("ffdf", c(physical(fdata), list(a=a)))

# physically combined columns
x<-ff(runif(10,0,1))
y<-as.ff(cbind(y=runif(10,-1,1), z=runif(10,2,3)))
fdata<-ffdf(x,y)
a <- clone(x)
fdata2 <- do.call("ffdf", c(physical(fdata), list(a=a)))
colnames(fdata2)[1:ncol(fdata)] <- colnames(fdata)

HTH

Jens

messages.body_plain:
I've been successfully using foreach for some basic problems, but I've run
into a new wrinkle that I think is due to me ignoring the .export and
.noexport flags.  My question is: is there any easy way to have foreach
ONLY export specific variables (ignoring all else) without having to
manually list them all in .noexport?

Also, once a variable has been .export 'ed in foreach, can it be used in
subsequent foreach calls  without calling a new .export (can I pre-load a
variable for use with multiple foreach'es)?

Thanks!

--jonathan

messages.subject: [R-sig-hpc] foreach .export and .noexport questions...
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Jonathan,

As with most things about foreach, it depends on the parallel backend. For
most of them,
where R sessions are initialized beforehand and hang around waiting for
work to do, the answer is "Yes". Remember, all that .export is trying to do
is make sure the things you need to run are available on the workers. So,
for those backends that are running R sessions just waiting for your jobs
to come to them, it is certainly possible to assign things into those
individual sessions and have them waiting for later commands. The odd duck
I know about is Revolution's own doRSR, where R sessions are initiated as
needed and don't stick around from one invocation of foreach to the next.

Cheers,
Rich

Makes sense -- What are your thoughts on adding a parameter such as
".exportifmissing" that will push an environment object to a worker if 1)
it has not already been exported or 2) the parallel backend doesn't support
"persistent" environments?  This would allow foreach to keep general
functionality while taking advantage of certain capabilities of some
backends?  The less attractive alternative (if I am trying to write general
code that takes advantage of foreach, while letting the user choose the
backend) would be to write a set of if/then statements querying the backend
type.

Cheers!

--jonathan

messages.subject: [R-sig-hpc] checkpointing with foreach
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

For a number of years, I've used my own 'mpifarm' package, which is
built on top of Rmpi, for parallel computing on clusters.  Recently,
I've been moving toward 'foreach', with its elegant syntax,
flexibility, and neat separation of back- and front-ends.

A few years ago, when I moved my HPC onto the university's big
cluster, I discovered that I could no longer live without some kind of
checkpointing facility.  Not so much because my codes were crashing,
though they sometimes were, but because it became necessary to submit
codes with small walltime requests in order to get scheduling priority
for big jobs in a sea of small, easily-scheduled jobs.  So I started
queueing up a number of instances of the same job, each with a modest
walltime request and the ability to read its predecessor's checkpoint
file and pick up where it left off.  This is all within-R
checkpointing for embarrassingly parallel problems: basically the
master looks for a checkpoint .rda file, loads it if it finds it, and
adjusts its to-do list accordingly.  It then updates the checkpoint
file from time to time.  I need this functionality in my new
'foreach'-based codes, and can think of several ways of doing it, not
all of which are likely to work on the first try.  Before I go about
reinventing that wheel, I wonder if anyone out there has come up with
a robust, flexible solution to checkpointing that's built on top of
'foreach'.   Or any advice?

Aaron

-- 
Aaron A. King, Ph.D.
Ecology & Evolutionary Biology
Mathematics
Center for the Study of Complex Systems
University of Michigan
